Management Summary

Threagile toolkit was used to model the architecture of "Water Treatment Plant" and derive risks by analyzing the components and data flows. The risks identified during this analysis are shown in the following chapters. Identified risks during threat modeling do not necessarily mean that the vulnerability associated with this risk actually exists: it is more to be seen as a list of potential risks and threats, which should be individually reviewed and reduced by removing false positives. For the remaining risks it should be checked in the design and implementation of "Water Treatment Plant" whether the mitigation advices have been applied or not.

Each risk finding references a chapter of the OWASP ASVS (Application Security Verification Standard) audit checklist. The OWASP ASVS checklist should be considered as an inspiration by architects and developers to further harden the application in a Defense-in-Depth approach. Additionally, for each risk finding a link towards a matching OWASP Cheat Sheet or similar with technical details about how to implement a mitigation is given.

Impact Analysis of the Initial Risks

The most prevalent impacts of the 43 initial risks (distributed over 14 risk categories) are (taking the severity ratings into account and using the highest for each category):

Elevated Direct IT/OT Communication: 1 Initial Risk, exploitation likelihood is Likely with High impact
If this risk is unmitigated, attackers who compromise an IT asset might reach the industrial control system and change, stop or damage the physical process it controls.
Elevated Human Use of Machine Identity: 1 Initial Risk, exploitation likelihood is Likely with High impact
If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might use a secret copied from a laptop, a script or a client to access the target, and nobody can tell who did what with it.

Application Overview

Business Criticality

The overall business criticality of "Water Treatment Plant" was rated as:

  • archive
  • operational
  • important
  • critical
  • mission-critical

Business Overview

The plant treats raw water into drinking water and pumps it to the town around the clock.

Technical Overview

A SCADA server supervises the dosing and filter PLCs and a remote pump station. A safety controller closes the chlorine supply on a leak. The corporate network reaches the plant through an industrial DMZ with a jump host and a replica of the historian.

Data-Flow Diagram

The following diagram was generated by Threagile based on the model input and gives a high-level overview of the data-flow between technical assets. The RAA value is the calculated Relative Attacker Attractiveness in percent.

Asset Register

Technical Assets

Chlorine Safety Controller
Closes the chlorine supply when a leak or an overdose is detected
Dosing PLC
Doses chlorine into the treated water
Engineering Workstation
Programs the PLCs, the RTU and the safety controller
Filter PLC
Runs the filters and their backwash
Jump Host
The only way into the plant network for remote access
Office Workstation
The workstations of the plant management in the corporate network
Operator HMI
The screens the operators run the plant with
Plant Historian
Archives the process values of the plant
Pump Station RTU
Runs the pumps of the remote pump station
SCADA Server
Supervises the treatment and sends the commands of the operators
Dosing Pump
The pump dosing the chlorine
Chlorine Analyzer
Measures the chlorine in the treated water
Chlorine Gas Detector
Detects chlorine gas in the dosing room
Historian Replica
A copy of the plant historian for the corporate network
Vendor Laptop out of scope
The laptops of the PLC vendor for remote support

Data Assets

Historical Process Data
Archived process values for reports and compliance
Process Values
Measurements of flow, level, pressure and chlorine concentration
Control Commands
Setpoints, start and stop commands and outputs to pumps and valves
Controller Programs
The logic and configuration of the PLCs and the RTU
Safety Logic
The program of the chlorine safety controller

Security Requirements

This chapter lists the custom security requirements which have been defined for the modeled target.

Safety Independence
The safety controller is changed only from a dedicated safety engineering workstation.
Zones and Conduits
IT reaches the plant only through the industrial DMZ.

This list is not complete and regulatory or law relevant security requirements have to be taken into account as well. Also custom individual security requirements might exist for the project.

Abuse Cases

This chapter lists the custom abuse cases which have been defined for the modeled target.

Chlorine Overdose
As an attacker I want to raise the chlorine setpoint of the dosing PLC to poison the drinking water.
Safety Bypass
As an attacker I want to disable the safety controller first, so that a chlorine leak goes unnoticed.
Supply Outage
As an attacker I want to stop the pumps of the pump station to cut the water supply of the town.

This list is not complete and regulatory or law relevant abuse cases have to be taken into account as well. Also custom individual abuse cases might exist for the project.

STRIDE Classification of Identified Risks

This chapter clusters and classifies the risks by STRIDE categories: in total 43 potential risks have been identified during the threat modeling process.

Spoofing 4 risks

Spoofing - Authenticity

Elevated Long-Lived Credentials: 3/3 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Likely with High impact
Passwords of service accounts, API keys and personal access tokens stay valid for months or for good. Once one leaks, from a repository, a log, a build system or a laptop, it lets anyone in until someone notices and rotates it.
Medium Long-Lived Credentials: 3/3 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Likely with High impact
Passwords of service accounts, API keys and personal access tokens stay valid for months or for good. Once one leaks, from a repository, a log, a build system or a laptop, it lets anyone in until someone notices and rotates it.
Medium Missing Identity Store: 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Medium impact
The modeled architecture does not contain an identity store, which might be the risk of a model missing critical assets (and thus not seeing their risks).

Tampering 12 risks

Tampering - Integrity

Elevated Insecure Control Protocol: 6/6 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Likely with Very High impact
Most industrial control protocols, like Modbus, DNP3, S7comm, EtherNet/IP or PROFINET, were designed for closed networks: a controller or field device executes every command it receives, without checking who sent it or whether it was changed on the way. Anyone who can send packets to it can write setpoints and outputs, stop it or download a new program.
Elevated Missing Hardening: 3/3 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Likely with Medium impact
Technical assets with a Relative Attacker Attractiveness (RAA) value of 55 % or higher should be explicitly hardened taking best practices and vendor hardening guides into account.
Elevated SQL/NoSQL-Injection: 3/3 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Very Likely with Medium impact
When a database is accessed via database access protocols SQL/NoSQL-Injection risks might arise. The risk rating depends on the sensitivity technical asset itself and of the data assets processed.
Medium Insecure Control Protocol: 6/6 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Likely with Very High impact
Most industrial control protocols, like Modbus, DNP3, S7comm, EtherNet/IP or PROFINET, were designed for closed networks: a controller or field device executes every command it receives, without checking who sent it or whether it was changed on the way. Anyone who can send packets to it can write setpoints and outputs, stop it or download a new program.
Medium Missing Hardening: 3/3 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Likely with Medium impact
Technical assets with a Relative Attacker Attractiveness (RAA) value of 55 % or higher should be explicitly hardened taking best practices and vendor hardening guides into account.

Repudiation 1 risk

Repudiation - Non-repudiability

Elevated Human Use of Machine Identity: 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Likely with High impact
People who call a service with the account of a machine, like an administrator using the credentials of a service account or a client that ships with an API key of its own, act without an identity of theirs. The service cannot tell them apart, nor require a second factor or end their access when they leave, and the secret gets copied to wherever they work.

Information Disclosure 13 risks

Information disclosure - Confidentiality

Elevated Unencrypted Communication: 10/10 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Likely with High impact
Due to the confidentiality and/or integrity rating of the data assets transferred over the communication link this connection must be encrypted.
Medium Missing Vault (Secret Storage): 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Medium impact
In order to avoid the risk of secret leakage via config files (when attacked through vulnerabilities being able to read files like Path-Traversal and others), it is best practice to use a separate hardened process with proper authentication, authorization, and audit logging to access config secrets (like credentials, private keys, client certificates, etc.). This component is usually some kind of Vault.
Medium Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF): 2/2 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Likely with Low impact
When a server system (i.e. not a client) is accessing other server systems via typical web protocols Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) or Local-File-Inclusion (LFI) or Remote-File-Inclusion (RFI) risks might arise.
Medium Unencrypted Communication: 10/10 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Likely with High impact
Due to the confidentiality and/or integrity rating of the data assets transferred over the communication link this connection must be encrypted.

Denial of Service 8 risks

Denial of service - Availability

Medium DoS-risky Access Across Trust-Boundary: 8/8 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Medium impact
Assets accessed across trust boundaries with critical or mission-critical availability rating are more prone to Denial-of-Service (DoS) risks.

Elevation of Privilege 5 risks

Elevation of privilege - Authorization

Elevated Direct IT/OT Communication: 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Likely with High impact
Controllers, field devices, HMIs, SCADA servers and engineering workstations of an industrial control system belong into control zones that IT assets reach only through an industrial DMZ. A direct communication link between an IT asset and an asset of a control zone lets attackers who compromise the IT side, which is far more exposed, move straight into the control of the physical process.
Elevated Missing Safety System Independence: 2/2 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Likely with Very High impact
A safety instrumented system brings the process into a safe state when the basic process control fails or is attacked. It only does so when it is independent of that control: when assets other than a dedicated safety engineering workstation can change its program, setpoints or outputs, one compromise can disable the control and the safety function together, as the TRITON attack did.
Elevated Unguarded Access From Internet: 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Very Likely with Medium impact
Internet-exposed assets must be guarded by a protecting service, application, or reverse-proxy.
Medium Missing Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA): 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Medium impact
Technical assets (especially multi-tenant systems) should authenticate incoming requests with multi-factor (MFA) authentication when the asset processes or stores highly sensitive data (in terms of confidentiality, integrity, and availability) and is accessed by humans.

Assignment by Function

This chapter clusters and assigns the risks by functions which are most likely able to check and mitigate them: in total 43 potential risks have been identified during the threat modeling process.

Business Side 1 risk

Business

Medium Missing Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA): 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Medium impact
Apply an authentication method to the technical asset protecting highly sensitive data via multi-factor authentication for human users.

Architecture 12 risks

Architecture

Elevated Direct IT/OT Communication: 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Likely with High impact
Separate IT and OT with an industrial DMZ, so that no communication link crosses from IT into a control zone directly: replicate the historian into the DMZ for IT users, give remote and vendor access only through a jump host there, and filter what passes with firewalls on both sides. Tag the assets in the DMZ with industrial-dmz.
Elevated Insecure Control Protocol: 6/6 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Likely with Very High impact
Use the secure variant of the protocol where the devices support it (Modbus/TCP Security, DNP3 over TLS or with Secure Authentication, CIP Security, OPC UA with SignAndEncrypt, S7comm-plus with access protection), and enable the access protection of the controllers. Where the protocol cannot be secured, allow only the expected senders and function codes with an industrial firewall in front of the controller, and keep controllers in RUN mode with the key switch.
Elevated Missing Safety System Independence: 2/2 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Likely with Very High impact
Let only a dedicated safety engineering workstation, which programs no other controllers, change the safety controller, and give the basic process control and the HMIs readonly access to its status. Keep the key switch of the safety controller in RUN mode outside of maintenance, and alert on every program change.
Elevated Unguarded Access From Internet: 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Very Likely with Medium impact
Encapsulate the asset behind a guarding service, application, or reverse-proxy. For admin maintenance a bastion-host should be used as a jump-server. For file transfer a store-and-forward-host should be used as an indirect file exchange platform.
Medium Insecure Control Protocol: 6/6 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Likely with Very High impact
Use the secure variant of the protocol where the devices support it (Modbus/TCP Security, DNP3 over TLS or with Secure Authentication, CIP Security, OPC UA with SignAndEncrypt, S7comm-plus with access protection), and enable the access protection of the controllers. Where the protocol cannot be secured, allow only the expected senders and function codes with an industrial firewall in front of the controller, and keep controllers in RUN mode with the key switch.
Medium Missing Identity Store: 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Medium impact
Include an identity store in the model if the application has a login.
Medium Missing Vault (Secret Storage): 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Medium impact
Consider using a Vault (Secret Storage) to securely store and access config secrets (like credentials, private keys, client certificates, etc.).

Development 5 risks

Development

Elevated SQL/NoSQL-Injection: 3/3 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Very Likely with Medium impact
Try to use parameter binding to be safe from injection vulnerabilities. When a third-party product is used instead of custom developed software, check if the product applies the proper mitigation and ensure a reasonable patch-level.
Medium Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF): 2/2 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Likely with Low impact
Try to avoid constructing the outgoing target URL with caller controllable values. Alternatively use a mapping (whitelist) when accessing outgoing URLs instead of creating them including caller controllable values. When a third-party product is used instead of custom developed software, check if the product applies the proper mitigation and ensure a reasonable patch-level.

Operations 25 risks

Operations

Elevated Human Use of Machine Identity: 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Likely with High impact
Let people sign in with their own identity, through single sign-on with multi-factor authentication, and pass it on to the target, modelling the link with the identity end-user. Where an administrator needs the permissions of a service, grant them for a limited time through a privileged access workflow that records who used them. Keep secrets of service accounts out of clients.
Elevated Long-Lived Credentials: 3/3 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Likely with High impact
Replace static secrets between services with a workload identity issued by the platform (cloud IAM roles, Kubernetes service account tokens, SPIFFE), or with short-lived tokens obtained through OAuth 2.0 client credentials or token exchange, and model the link with the identity workload or the authentication short-lived-token. Where a long-lived secret remains, keep it in a vault, scope it narrowly, rotate it automatically and detect its use from unexpected places.
Elevated Missing Hardening: 3/3 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Likely with Medium impact
Try to apply all hardening best practices (like CIS benchmarks, OWASP recommendations, vendor recommendations, DevSec Hardening Framework, DBSAT for Oracle databases, and others).
Elevated Unencrypted Communication: 10/10 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Likely with High impact
Apply transport layer encryption to the communication link.
Medium DoS-risky Access Across Trust-Boundary: 8/8 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Medium impact
Apply anti-DoS techniques like throttling and/or per-client load blocking with quotas. Also for maintenance access routes consider applying a VPN instead of public reachable interfaces. Generally applying redundancy on the targeted technical asset reduces the risk of DoS.

RAA Analysis

For each technical asset the "Relative Attacker Attractiveness" (RAA) value was calculated in percent. The higher the RAA, the more interesting it is for an attacker to compromise the asset. The calculation algorithm takes the sensitivity ratings and quantities of stored and processed data into account as well as the communication links of the technical asset. Neighbouring assets to high-value RAA targets might receive an increase in their RAA value when they have a communication link towards that target ("Pivoting-Factor").

The following lists all technical assets sorted by their RAA value from highest (most attacker attractive) to lowest. This list can be used to prioritize on efforts relevant for the most attacker-attractive technical assets:

SCADA Server: RAA 100 % Elevated
Supervises the treatment and sends the commands of the operators
Plant Historian: RAA 63 % Elevated
Archives the process values of the plant
Dosing PLC: RAA 59 % Elevated
Doses chlorine into the treated water
Engineering Workstation: RAA 55 % Elevated
Programs the PLCs, the RTU and the safety controller
Operator HMI: RAA 53 % Elevated
The screens the operators run the plant with
Chlorine Safety Controller: RAA 52 % Elevated
Closes the chlorine supply when a leak or an overdose is detected
Filter PLC: RAA 46 % Elevated
Runs the filters and their backwash
Office Workstation: RAA 37 % Elevated
The workstations of the plant management in the corporate network
Historian Replica: RAA 36 %
A copy of the plant historian for the corporate network
Jump Host: RAA 33 % Elevated
The only way into the plant network for remote access
Pump Station RTU: RAA 33 % Elevated
Runs the pumps of the remote pump station

The pump dosing the chlorine

This chapter lists potential model failures where not all relevant assets have been modeled or the model might itself contain inconsistencies. Each potential model failure should be checked in the model against the architecture design:

Elevated Direct IT/OT Communication: 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Likely with High impact
Controllers, field devices, HMIs, SCADA servers and engineering workstations of an industrial control system belong into control zones that IT assets reach only through an industrial DMZ. A direct communication link between an IT asset and an asset of a control zone lets attackers who compromise the IT side, which is far more exposed, move straight into the control of the physical process.
Medium Missing Identity Store: 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Medium impact
The modeled architecture does not contain an identity store, which might be the risk of a model missing critical assets (and thus not seeing their risks).
Medium Missing Vault (Secret Storage): 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Medium impact
In order to avoid the risk of secret leakage via config files (when attacked through vulnerabilities being able to read files like Path-Traversal and others), it is best practice to use a separate hardened process with proper authentication, authorization, and audit logging to access config secrets (like credentials, private keys, client certificates, etc.). This component is usually some kind of Vault.

Direct IT/OT Communication Elevated 1/1 unmitigated Risk

direct-it-ot-communication

STRIDEElevation of Privilege
CWECWE 1008
FunctionArchitecture
ActionIndustrial DMZ
ASVS chapterV1 - Architecture, Design and Threat Modeling Requirements
Cheat sheetfinal
ReferencesIEC 62443-3-3 SR 5.1 Network Segmentation; IEC 62443-3-3 SR 5.2 Zone Boundary Protection; MITRE ATT&CK for ICS T0883 Internet Accessible Device; MITRE ATT&CK for ICS T0886 Remote Services; NIST SP 800-82r3 Guide to Operational Technology (OT) Security

Description

Controllers, field devices, HMIs, SCADA servers and engineering workstations of an industrial control system belong into control zones that IT assets reach only through an industrial DMZ. A direct communication link between an IT asset and an asset of a control zone lets attackers who compromise the IT side, which is far more exposed, move straight into the control of the physical process.

Impact

If this risk is unmitigated, attackers who compromise an IT asset might reach the industrial control system and change, stop or damage the physical process it controls.

Detection Logic

In-scope OT technical assets (plc, rtu, safety-controller, field-device, hmi, scada-server, engineering-workstation) with a communication link, in either direction, with a technical asset that is neither an OT asset nor in the industrial DMZ (a historian or an asset tagged with industrial-dmz).

Risk Rating

The risk rating depends on the integrity and availability of the OT asset, and is the highest for safety controllers. The attack is very likely when the other asset is on the internet, and likely otherwise.

False Positives

Links that pass through a firewall allowing only them, and that are documented exceptions of the zone model, can be considered as false positives after individual review.

Mitigation

Separate IT and OT with an industrial DMZ, so that no communication link crosses from IT into a control zone directly: replicate the historian into the DMZ for IT users, give remote and vendor access only through a jump host there, and filter what passes with firewalls on both sides. Tag the assets in the DMZ with industrial-dmz.

Check

Are the recommendations of NIST SP 800-82 and the referenced IEC 62443 requirements applied?

Human Use of Machine Identity Elevated 1/1 unmitigated Risk

human-use-of-machine-identity

STRIDERepudiation
CWECWE 1390
FunctionOperations

ASVS chapterV2 - Authentication Verification Requirements
Cheat sheetSecrets_Management_Cheat_Sheet
ReferencesOWASP A07:2025 Authentication Failures; OWASP NHI10:2025 Human Use of NHI; OWASP ASI03:2026 Identity and Privilege Abuse

Description

People who call a service with the account of a machine, like an administrator using the credentials of a service account or a client that ships with an API key of its own, act without an identity of theirs. The service cannot tell them apart, nor require a second factor or end their access when they leave, and the secret gets copied to wherever they work.

Impact

If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might use a secret copied from a laptop, a script or a client to access the target, and nobody can tell who did what with it.

Detection Logic

In-scope technical assets processing or storing data rated at least as confidential or critical with an incoming communication link that is not process-local, from a caller used by humans, whose identity is service-account or workload.

Risk Rating

The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the data processed or stored by the target. The attack is likely, as secrets in the hands of people leak easily.

False Positives

Clients whose users sign in with their own identity first, which a service then exchanges for the narrowly scoped account of the client, can be considered as false positives after individual review.

Mitigation

Let people sign in with their own identity, through single sign-on with multi-factor authentication, and pass it on to the target, modelling the link with the identity end-user. Where an administrator needs the permissions of a service, grant them for a limited time through a privileged access workflow that records who used them. Keep secrets of service accounts out of clients.

Check

Are recommendations from the linked cheat sheet and referenced ASVS chapter applied?

Insecure Control Protocol Elevated 6/6 unmitigated Risks

insecure-control-protocol

STRIDETampering
CWECWE 306
FunctionArchitecture
ActionAuthenticated Control Protocols
ASVS chapterV1 - Architecture, Design and Threat Modeling Requirements
Cheat sheetfinal
ReferencesIEC 62443-3-3 SR 1.2 Software Process and Device Identification and Authentication; IEC 62443-3-3 SR 3.1 Communication Integrity; MITRE ATT&CK for ICS T0855 Unauthorized Command Message; MITRE ATT&CK for ICS T0830 Adversary-in-the-Middle; NIST SP 800-82r3 Guide to Operational Technology (OT) Security

Description

Most industrial control protocols, like Modbus, DNP3, S7comm, EtherNet/IP or PROFINET, were designed for closed networks: a controller or field device executes every command it receives, without checking who sent it or whether it was changed on the way. Anyone who can send packets to it can write setpoints and outputs, stop it or download a new program.

Impact

If this risk is unmitigated, attackers in the network might send commands that change, stop or damage the physical process, or alter the commands and readings exchanged with the controller.

Detection Logic

In-scope controllers (plc, rtu, safety-controller) and field-device technical assets with an incoming non-readonly communication link over an industrial control protocol without a secure variant in use (all of them except modbus-security, dnp3-encrypted and opc-ua-encrypted).

Risk Rating

The risk rating depends on the integrity and availability of the controlled process, and is the highest for safety controllers. The attack is very likely when the sender is on the internet, likely when it is an IT asset, reaches IT or calls across a network trust boundary, and unlikely otherwise.

False Positives

Links in an isolated network that only the sender and the receiver are part of can be considered as false positives after individual review.

Mitigation

Use the secure variant of the protocol where the devices support it (Modbus/TCP Security, DNP3 over TLS or with Secure Authentication, CIP Security, OPC UA with SignAndEncrypt, S7comm-plus with access protection), and enable the access protection of the controllers. Where the protocol cannot be secured, allow only the expected senders and function codes with an industrial firewall in front of the controller, and keep controllers in RUN mode with the key switch.

Check

Are the recommendations of NIST SP 800-82 and the referenced IEC 62443 requirements applied?

Description

Passwords of service accounts, API keys and personal access tokens stay valid for months or for good. Once one leaks, from a repository, a log, a build system or a laptop, it lets anyone in until someone notices and rotates it.

Impact

If this risk is unmitigated, attackers who find a leaked secret might use it for a long time to access the target with the permissions of the caller.

Detection Logic

In-scope technical assets processing or storing data rated at least as confidential or critical with an incoming communication link that is not process-local and is authenticated with long-lived-token, or with credentials by a caller not used by humans, unless the identity of the link is workload. Links authenticated with token are skipped, as the lifetime of the token is not modelled.

Risk Rating

The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the data processed or stored by the target. The attack is likely when the caller is on the internet, is used by humans or calls across a network trust boundary, where secrets leak more easily, and unlikely otherwise.

False Positives

Secrets that are rotated automatically within hours can be considered as false positives after individual review.

Mitigation

Replace static secrets between services with a workload identity issued by the platform (cloud IAM roles, Kubernetes service account tokens, SPIFFE), or with short-lived tokens obtained through OAuth 2.0 client credentials or token exchange, and model the link with the identity workload or the authentication short-lived-token. Where a long-lived secret remains, keep it in a vault, scope it narrowly, rotate it automatically and detect its use from unexpected places.

Check

Are recommendations from the linked cheat sheet and referenced ASVS chapter applied?

Missing Safety System Independence Elevated 2/2 unmitigated Risks

missing-safety-system-independence

STRIDEElevation of Privilege
CWECWE 284
FunctionArchitecture
ActionSafety System Independence
ASVS chapterV1 - Architecture, Design and Threat Modeling Requirements
Cheat sheetfinal
ReferencesIEC 61511 Independence of the Safety Instrumented System; MITRE ATT&CK for ICS T0880 Loss of Safety; MITRE ATT&CK for ICS T0843 Program Download; IEC 62443-3-3 SR 5.1 Network Segmentation; NIST SP 800-82r3 Guide to Operational Technology (OT) Security

Description

A safety instrumented system brings the process into a safe state when the basic process control fails or is attacked. It only does so when it is independent of that control: when assets other than a dedicated safety engineering workstation can change its program, setpoints or outputs, one compromise can disable the control and the safety function together, as the TRITON attack did.

Impact

If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might disable or trip the safety function and so cause explosions, releases of hazardous material or injuries.

Detection Logic

In-scope safety-controller technical assets with an incoming non-readonly communication link that is not process-local, from a technical asset other than an engineering-workstation that has no non-readonly communication links to other controllers.

Risk Rating

The impact is very high, as the safety function protects people. The attack is very likely when the sender is on the internet, likely when it is an IT asset, reaches IT or calls across a network trust boundary, and unlikely otherwise.

False Positives

Links whose writes the safety controller itself restricts to values that cannot impair the safety function can be considered as false positives after individual review.

Mitigation

Let only a dedicated safety engineering workstation, which programs no other controllers, change the safety controller, and give the basic process control and the HMIs readonly access to its status. Keep the key switch of the safety controller in RUN mode outside of maintenance, and alert on every program change.

Check

Are the recommendations of NIST SP 800-82 and the referenced IEC 62443 requirements applied?

Unguarded Access From Internet Elevated 1/1 unmitigated Risk

unguarded-access-from-internet

STRIDEElevation of Privilege
CWECWE 501
FunctionArchitecture
ActionEncapsulation of Technical Asset
ASVS chapterV1 - Architecture, Design and Threat Modeling Requirements
Cheat sheetAttack_Surface_Analysis_Cheat_Sheet
ReferencesOWASP A06:2025 Insecure Design

Description

Internet-exposed assets must be guarded by a protecting service, application, or reverse-proxy.

Impact

If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might be able to directly attack sensitive systems without any hardening components in-between due to them being directly exposed on the internet.

Detection Logic

In-scope technical assets (excluding load-balancer) with confidentiality rating of confidential (or higher) or with integrity rating of critical (or higher) when accessed directly from the internet. All web-server, web-application, reverse-proxy, waf, and gateway assets are exempted from this risk when they do not consist of custom developed code and the data-flow only consists of HTTP or FTP protocols. Access from monitoring systems as well as VPN-protected connections are exempted.

Risk Rating

The matching technical assets are at low risk. When either the confidentiality rating is strictly-confidential or the integrity rating is mission-critical, the risk-rating is considered medium. For assets with RAA values higher than 40 % the risk-rating increases.

False Positives

When other means of filtering client requests are applied equivalent of reverse-proxy, waf, or gateway components.

Mitigation

Encapsulate the asset behind a guarding service, application, or reverse-proxy. For admin maintenance a bastion-host should be used as a jump-server. For file transfer a store-and-forward-host should be used as an indirect file exchange platform.

Check

dos-risky-access-across-trust-boundary

ASVS chapterV1 - Architecture, Design and Threat Modeling Requirements
Cheat sheetDenial_of_Service_Cheat_Sheet
ReferencesOWASP API4:2023 Unrestricted Resource Consumption

Description

Assets accessed across trust boundaries with critical or mission-critical availability rating are more prone to Denial-of-Service (DoS) risks.

Impact

If this risk remains unmitigated, attackers might be able to disturb the availability of important parts of the system.

Detection Logic

In-scope technical assets (excluding load-balancer) with availability rating of critical or higher which have incoming data-flows across a network trust-boundary (excluding devops usage).

Risk Rating

Matching technical assets with availability rating of critical or higher are at low risk. When the availability rating is mission-critical and neither a VPN nor IP filter for the incoming data-flow nor redundancy for the asset is applied, the risk-rating is considered medium.

False Positives

When the accessed target operations are not time- or resource-consuming.

Mitigation

Apply anti-DoS techniques like throttling and/or per-client load blocking with quotas. Also for maintenance access routes consider applying a VPN instead of public reachable interfaces. Generally applying redundancy on the targeted technical asset reduces the risk of DoS.

Description

Technical assets (especially multi-tenant systems) should authenticate incoming requests with multi-factor (MFA) authentication when the asset processes or stores highly sensitive data (in terms of confidentiality, integrity, and availability) and is accessed by humans.

Impact

If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might be able to access or modify highly sensitive data without strong authentication.

Detection Logic

In-scope technical assets (except load-balancer, reverse-proxy, waf, ids, and ips) should authenticate incoming requests via multi-factor authentication (MFA) when the asset processes or stores highly sensitive data (in terms of confidentiality, integrity, and availability) and is accessed by a client used by a human user. Links over industrial control protocols that cannot authenticate are left to the insecure-control-protocol rule.

Risk Rating

medium

False Positives

Technical assets which do not process requests regarding functionality or data linked to end-users (customers) can be considered as false positives after individual review.

Mitigation

Apply an authentication method to the technical asset protecting highly sensitive data via multi-factor authentication for human users.

Description

In order to avoid the risk of secret leakage via config files (when attacked through vulnerabilities being able to read files like Path-Traversal and others), it is best practice to use a separate hardened process with proper authentication, authorization, and audit logging to access config secrets (like credentials, private keys, client certificates, etc.). This component is usually some kind of Vault.

Impact

If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might be able to easier steal config secrets (like credentials, private keys, client certificates, etc.) once a vulnerability to access files is present and exploited.

Detection Logic

Models without a Vault (Secret Storage).

Risk Rating

The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the technical asset itself and of the data assets processed.

False Positives

Models where no technical assets have any kind of sensitive config data to protect can be considered as false positives after individual review.

Mitigation

Consider using a Vault (Secret Storage) to securely store and access config secrets (like credentials, private keys, client certificates, etc.).

Check

GetAttribute a Vault (Secret Storage) in place?

Description

When a server system (i.e. not a client) is accessing other server systems via typical web protocols Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) or Local-File-Inclusion (LFI) or Remote-File-Inclusion (RFI) risks might arise.

Impact

If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might be able to access sensitive services or files of network-reachable components by modifying outgoing calls of affected components.

Detection Logic

In-scope non-client systems accessing (using outgoing communication links) targets with either HTTP or HTTPS protocol.

Risk Rating

The risk rating (low or medium) depends on the sensitivity of the data assets receivable via web protocols from targets within the same network trust-boundary as well on the sensitivity of the data assets receivable via web protocols from the target asset itself. Also for cloud-based environments the exploitation impact is at least medium, as cloud backend services can be attacked via SSRF.

False Positives

Servers not sending outgoing web requests can be considered as false positives after review.

Mitigation

Try to avoid constructing the outgoing target URL with caller controllable values. Alternatively use a mapping (whitelist) when accessing outgoing URLs instead of creating them including caller controllable values. When a third-party product is used instead of custom developed software, check if the product applies the proper mitigation and ensure a reasonable patch-level.

Check

Threagile (see threagile.io for more details) is an open-source toolkit for agile threat modeling, created by Christian Schneider (christian-schneider.net): It allows to model an architecture with its assets in an agile fashion as a YAML file directly inside the IDE. Upon execution of the Threagile toolkit all standard risk rules (as well as individual custom rules if present) are checked against the architecture model. At the time the Threagile toolkit was executed on the model input file the following risk rules were checked:

Risk ruleSTRIDEDescriptionDetectionRating
Accidental Secret Leak
accidental-secret-leak		Information DisclosureSourcecode repositories (including their histories) as well as artifact registries can accidentally contain secrets like checked-in or packaged-in passwords, API tokens, certificates, crypto keys, etc.In-scope sourcecode repositories and artifact registries.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the technical asset itself and of the data assets processed.
Code Backdooring
code-backdooring		TamperingFor each build pipeline component Code Backdooring risks might arise where attackers compromise the build pipeline in order to let backdoored artifacts be shipped into production. Aside from direct code backdooring this includes backdooring of dependencies and even of more lower-level build infrastructure, like backdooring compilers (similar to what the XcodeGhost malware did) or dependencies.In-scope development relevant technical assets which are either accessed by out-of-scope unmanaged developer clients and/or are directly accessed by any kind of internet-located (non-VPN) component or are themselves directly located on the internet.The risk rating depends on the confidentiality and integrity rating of the code being handled and deployed as well as the placement/calling of this technical asset on/from the internet.
Confused Deputy Agent
confused-deputy-agent		Elevation of PrivilegeAn AI agent that acts for its users but reaches data and tools with an identity of its own, a service account or a workload, can do for any user what the agent may do for all of them. The targets check the agent, not the user, so whatever a user asks for, or a prompt injection makes the agent ask for, is allowed.In-scope ai-agent technical assets that act for users, through an incoming communication link with the identity end-user or from a caller used by humans (other than devops links), and reach a technical asset (other than an llm) processing or storing data rated at least as confidential or critical with the identity service-account or workload, either directly or through the tools of an mcp-server technical asset.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the most sensitive technical asset the agent reaches with its own identity. The attack is likely when the agent takes untrusted input, and unlikely otherwise.
Container Base Image Backdooring
container-baseimage-backdooring		TamperingWhen a technical asset is built using container technologies, Base Image Backdooring risks might arise where base images and other layers used contain vulnerable components or backdoors.In-scope technical assets running as containers, other than external entities. To track the risks of all containers at once, use the risk tracking key container-baseimage-backdooring@*.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the technical asset itself and of the data assets.
Container Platform Escape
container-platform-escape		Elevation of PrivilegeContainer platforms are especially interesting targets for attackers as they host big parts of a containerized runtime infrastructure. When not configured and operated with security best practices in mind, attackers might exploit a vulnerability inside an container and escape towards the platform as highly privileged users. These scenarios might give attackers capabilities to attack every other container as owning the container platform (via container escape attacks) equals to owning every container.In-scope container platforms.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the technical asset itself and of the data assets processed.
Cross-Account Takeover
cross-account-takeover		Elevation of PrivilegeCloud accounts, subscriptions, projects and VPCs isolate workloads and tenants from each other. Access from one of them into another (account A to account B) is granted by cross-account roles, trust policies or resource policies, and a misconfigured grant (too broad principals or rights, or no condition on the calling account) breaks that isolation.Communication links into in-scope technical assets from technical assets in another cloud account, i.e. where the innermost trust boundaries of type network-cloud-provider around the source and the target differ.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the target technical asset itself and of the data assets it processes and stores. The likelihood rises when the source or the target is multi-tenant, as another tenant can then try to abuse the cross-account access.
Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
cross-site-request-forgery		SpoofingWhen a web application is accessed via web protocols Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) risks might arise.In-scope web applications accessed via typical web access protocols by a caller used by humans or a browser, directly or through technical assets forwarding the traffic, like load balancers, reverse proxies and WAFs. Requests of other callers, like a backend or a batch job, come from no browser a forged request could use, and are skipped.The risk rating depends on the integrity rating of the data sent across the communication link. The attack is very likely, likely for DevOps usage, and unlikely when the link is authenticated with a token (token, short-lived-token or long-lived-token), which a browser does not send on its own like a cookie.
Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
cross-site-scripting		TamperingFor each web application Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) risks might arise. In terms of the overall risk level take other applications running on the same domain into account as well.In-scope web applications.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the data processed in the web application.
Direct IT/OT Communication
direct-it-ot-communication		Elevation of PrivilegeControllers, field devices, HMIs, SCADA servers and engineering workstations of an industrial control system belong into control zones that IT assets reach only through an industrial DMZ. A direct communication link between an IT asset and an asset of a control zone lets attackers who compromise the IT side, which is far more exposed, move straight into the control of the physical process.In-scope OT technical assets (plc, rtu, safety-controller, field-device, hmi, scada-server, engineering-workstation) with a communication link, in either direction, with a technical asset that is neither an OT asset nor in the industrial DMZ (a historian or an asset tagged with industrial-dmz).The risk rating depends on the integrity and availability of the OT asset, and is the highest for safety controllers. The attack is very likely when the other asset is on the internet, and likely otherwise.

unsandboxed-code-execution		Elevation of PrivilegeA code interpreter runs the code that a language model or an AI agent writes. When untrusted content reaches the model, a prompt injection decides what that code does, and the code can do whatever the interpreter can reach: the systems it has links to, the internet, and the other assets of the runtime it shares, or all of the agent when it runs inside it.In-scope code-interpreter technical assets that a language model or an AI agent taking untrusted content (as for prompt injection) sends code to, or that are such a model or agent themselves, when the code can reach data rated at least as confidential or critical: through a link of the interpreter, in an asset of a shared runtime it runs in, by sending what it processes to an internet asset, or, inside an agent, through what the agent processes and can change.The risk rating depends on the most sensitive data the code can reach. The attack is very likely when the model or agent writing the code talks to the internet directly, and likely otherwise.
Untrusted Deserialization
untrusted-deserialization		TamperingWhen a technical asset accepts data in a specific serialized form (like Java or .NET serialization), Untrusted Deserialization risks might arise.In-scope technical assets accepting serialization data formats (including EJB and RMI protocols).The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the technical asset itself and of the data assets processed.
Vector Store Poisoning
vector-store-poisoning		TamperingLanguage models and agents answer and act on what they retrieve from vector stores, for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) or as the memory of an agent. Whoever can write into the store decides what the model believes: a poisoned document or memory entry carries false facts or hidden instructions into every answer that retrieves it, long after it was written.In-scope vector-database technical assets that an llm or ai-agent technical asset communicates with.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the data processed by the models and agents that use the store. The attack is likely when the store is written by an asset that takes untrusted input or sits across a network trust boundary, and unlikely otherwise.
Wrong Communication Link Content
wrong-communication-link-content		Information DisclosureWhen a communication link is defined as readonly, but does not receive any data asset, or when it is defined as not readonly, but does not send any data asset, it is likely to be a model failure.Communication links with inconsistent data assets being sent/received not matching their readonly flag or otherwise inconsistent protocols not matching the target technology type.low
Wrong Trust Boundary Content
wrong-trust-boundary-content		Elevation of PrivilegeWhen a trust boundary of type network-policy-namespace-isolation contains non-container assets it is likely to be a model failure.Trust boundaries which should only contain containers, but have different assets inside.low
XML External Entity (XXE)
xml-external-entity		Information DisclosureWhen a technical asset accepts data in XML format, XML External Entity (XXE) risks might arise.In-scope technical assets accepting XML data formats.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the technical asset itself and of the data assets processed. Also for cloud-based environments the exploitation impact is at least medium, as cloud backend services can be attacked via SSRF (and XXE vulnerabilities are often also SSRF vulnerabilities).
